arxiv-2206-01643.title: ChaTEAU: A Universal Toolkit for Applying the Chase
arxiv-2206-01643.creator: Tanja Auge, Nic Scharlau, Andreas Görres, Jakob Zimmer, Andreas Heuer
arxiv-2206-01643.description: Abstract . What do applications like semantic optimization, data exchange and integration, answering queries under dependencies, query reformulation with constraints, and data cleaning have in common? All these applications can be processed by the Chase , a family of algorithms for reasoning with constraints.

arxiv-2209-02007.title: Stop the [Image] Steal: The Role and Dynamics of Visual Content in the 2020 U.S. Election Misinformation Campaign Journal: PACMHCI Volume: 6 CSCW2 541 11 Price: 15.00 DOI: 10.1145/3555599 CCS: Human-centered computing Empirical studies in collaborative and social computing CCS: Human-centered comput
arxiv-2209-02007.creator: Hana Matatov, Mor Naaman, Ofra Amir
arxiv-2209-02007.description: Abstract . Images are powerful. Visual information can attract attention, improve persuasion, trigger stronger emotions, and is easy to share and spread. We examine the characteristics of the popular images shared on Twitter as part of “Stop the Steal”, the widespread misinformation campaign during the 2020 U.S. election.

arxiv-2405-20126.title: Federated and Transfer Learning for Cancer Detection Based on Image Analysis
arxiv-2405-20126.creator: Amine Bechar, Youssef Elmir, Yassine Himeur, Rafik Medjoudj, Abbes Amira
arxiv-2405-20126.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Amine Bechar, Youssef Elmir, Yassine Himeur, Rafik Medjoudj, Abbes Amira. This review article discusses the roles of federated learning (FL) and transfer learning (TL) in cancer detection based on image analysis. These two strategies powered by machine learning have drawn a lot of attention due to their potential to increase the precision and effectiveness of cancer diagnosis in light of the growing importance of machine learning techniques in cancer detection.

arxiv-2501-10274.title: Genuine Multipartite Nonlocality sharing under Sequential Measurement
arxiv-2501-10274.creator: Sk Sahadat Hossain, Indrani Chattopadhyay
arxiv-2501-10274.description: Abstract The study of quantum nonlocality sharing has garnered significant attention, particularly for two-qubit and three-qubit entangled systems. In this paper, we extend the investigation to n n -qubit Greenberger-Horne-Zeilinger (GHZ) systems ( OPEN n ≥ 4 ) n\geq 4) , analyzing nonlocality sharing under unbiased unsharp measurements.

arxiv-2506-17193.title: Any nonincreasing convergence curves are simultaneously possible for GMRES and weighted GMRES, as well as for left and right preconditioned GMRES This work was supported in part by the ANR project DARK (research grant ANR-24-CE46-1633).
arxiv-2506-17193.creator: P. Matalon, N. Spillane
arxiv-2506-17193.description: Abstract The convergence of the GMRES linear solver is notoriously hard to predict. A particularly enlightening result by [Greenbaum, Pták, Strakoš, 1996] is that, given any convergence curve, one can build a linear system for which GMRES realizes that convergence curve. What is even more extraordinary is that the eigenvalues of the problem matrix can be chosen arbitrarily.

arxiv-2507-20262.title: Future Parameter Constraints from Weak Lensing CMB and Galaxy Lensing Power- and Bispectra
arxiv-2507-20262.creator: P. Daniel Meerburg
arxiv-2507-20262.description: Abstract Upcoming stage 4 surveys, such as the Simons Observatory, LSST, and Euclid, are poised to measure weak gravitational lensing of the Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB) and galaxies with unprecedented precision. While the power spectrum is the standard statistic used to analyze weak lensing data, non-Gaussianity from non-linear structure growth encodes additional cosmological information in higher-order statistics.

arxiv-2512-08495.title: Supervised Classification of LEO Debris Families Using Multi-Set Proper Elements
arxiv-2512-08495.creator: Michael Ling
arxiv-2512-08495.description: Abstract The use of proper elements to reconnect families of satellite fragmentation debris has recently advanced with the emergence of machine learning techniques. These developments are key to improving the efficiency and effectiveness of operations in space sustainability operations, collision avoidance, and space domain awareness.

pmc-11318238.title: A social media game to increase physical activity among older adult women: protocol of a randomized controlled trial to evaluate CHALLENGE
pmc-11318238.creator: Michael C Robertson, Maria Chang Swartz, Karen M Basen-Engquist, Yisheng Li, Kristofer Jennings, Debbe Thompson, Tom Baranowski, Elena Volpi, Elizabeth J Lyons
pmc-11318238.description: BackgroundOlder adult women often do not engage in sufficient physical activity (PA) and can encounter biological changes that exacerbate the negative effects of inadequate activity. Wearable activity monitors can facilitate PA initiation, but evidence of sustained behavior change is lacking.

pmc-11424489.title: Forest fire size amplifies postfire land surface warming
pmc-11424489.creator: Jie Zhao, Chao Yue, Jiaming Wang, Stijn Hantson, Xianli Wang, Binbin He, Guangyao Li, Liang Wang, Hongfei Zhao, Sebastiaan Luyssaert
pmc-11424489.description: Climate warming has caused a widespread increase in extreme fire weather, making forest fires longer-lived and larger1–3. The average forest fire size in Canada, the USA and Australia has doubled or even tripled in recent decades4,5. In return, forest fires feed back to climate by modulating land–atmospheric carbon, nitrogen, aerosol, energy and water fluxes6–8.

pmc-11600746.title: Risk factors for low back pain amongst adults in Nigeria and South Africa: a systematic review
pmc-11600746.creator: Matthew Fay, Michelle Black
pmc-11600746.description: BackgroundThe burden on the individual, society and healthcare providers of low back pain in the western world is well documented. Globalisation and urbanisation, it has been reported, has led to an increase in low back pain in developing countries such as those situated in Sub-Saharan Africa. Low back pain determinants are framed, according to the individual, social and cultural context.

pmc-11605943.title: Determinants of life satisfaction in adolescents with congenital or acquired heart disease: a nationwide cross-sectional study
pmc-11605943.creator: Mohamad El-Chouli, Sidsel Marie Bernt Jørgensen, Daniel Mølager Christensen, Isabella Drachmann, Thomas Steen Gyldenstierne Sehested, Morten Winther Malmborg, Sandra Chamat-Hedemand, Caroline Sindet-Pedersen, Lars Idorn, Gunnar Hilmar Gislason, Thomas Alexander Gerds, Susan Ishøy Michelsen, Nina Føn
pmc-11605943.description: BackgroundWe aimed to investigate how self-reported physical and cognitive limitations (challenges), self-efficacy, and social support interacted with life satisfaction in adolescents and young adults with congenital heart disease (CHD) or acquired heart disease, among whom life satisfaction may be impaired.Methods“Adolescence with Heart Disease” was a cross-sectional, nationwide survey of patients with CHD or early acquired heart disease aged 15–25.

pmc-12631608.title: Explainable detection: a transformer-based language modeling approach for Bengali news title classification with comparative explainability analysis using ML and DL
pmc-12631608.creator: Md. Julkar Naeen, Sourav Kumar Das, Sakib Alam Jisan, Sharun Akter Khushbu, Noyon Chandra Saha, Ohidujjaman
pmc-12631608.description: Classifying scattered Bengali text is the primary focus of this study, with an emphasis on explainability in Natural Language Processing (NLP) for low-resource languages. We employed supervised Machine Learning (ML) models as a baseline and compared their performance with Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks from the deep learning domain. Subsequently, we implemented transformer models designed for sequential learning.

pmc-13047794.title: Descemet membrane endothelial keratoplasty in patients after radiation therapy for uveal melanoma
pmc-13047794.creator: Anna-Karina B Maier, Dhoksina Papa, Aline Riechardt, Jens Heufelder, Oliver Zeitz, Antonia M Joussen, Tina Dietrich-Ntoukas
pmc-13047794.description: PurposeTo evaluate the visual outcomes and postoperative complications after Descemet membrane endothelial keratoplasty (DMEK) in patients after radiation therapy for uveal melanoma.MethodsIn this retrospective observational study, 9 eyes of 9 patients after radiation therapy for uveal melanoma who received DMEK surgery at the Charité – Universitätsmedizin Berlin were included. Preoperative patients` characteristics were analyzed.

pmc-13207907.title: Accuracy of Intraocular Lens Power Calculation in Cataract Surgery Combined with Trabeculectomy in Open Angle Glaucoma
pmc-13207907.creator: Giulia Coco, Giulia Piccotti, Federica Genova, Lucrezia Leucci, Danilo Iannetta, Gloria Roberti, Carlo Nucci
pmc-13207907.description: Background/Objectives: To assess the accuracy of several intraocular lens power calculation formulas in phacotrabeculectomy for open angle glaucoma. Methods: Patients who underwent phacotrabeculectomy for open angle glaucoma were included. Refraction and biometry measurements were repeated at 3, 6 and ≥12 months.

pmc-13360037.creator: Baptiste Morcel, Youri Yordanov, Eric Mercier, Jean-Stéphane David, Tobias Gauss, Karim Tazarourte, Axel Benhamed
pmc-13360037.description: BackgroundWhile volume–outcome relationships for non-traumatic out-of-hospital cardiac arrest have been reported in hospital settings, the impact of prehospital exposure, particularly for the rare and clinically complex entity of traumatic cardiac arrest (TCA), remains uncertain and may influence emergency medical services (EMS) proficiency and survival.
